q: Coordination involves two main body systems: the endocrine system and the _____ system, which is involved in the transmission of nerve impulses.
e: Coordination involves two main body systems: the endocrine system and the nervous system, which is involved in the transmission of nerve impulses. The blank is nervous. Not respiratory or digestive.

q: The central nervous system is composed of the spinal cord and the _____.
e: The central nervous system is composed of the spinal cord and the brain. The blank is brain. Not heart or liver.

q: The forebrain comprises the cerebrum, thalamus, and hypothalamus, while the hindbrain consists of the cerebellum, pons, and _____.
e: The forebrain comprises the cerebrum, thalamus, and hypothalamus, while the hindbrain consists of the cerebellum, pons, and medulla oblongata. So we write medulla oblongata. Leave cerebellum and pons out.

q: The meninges are three layers of tough, elastic tissue within the skull and spinal column that directly enclose and _____ the brain and spinal cord.
e: The meninges are three layers of tough, elastic tissue within the skull and spinal column that directly enclose and protect the brain and spinal cord. Protect is the word, not nourish or support.

q: The thalamus acts as the great _____ station of the brain, providing connections between various parts of the brain.
e: The thalamus acts as the great relay station of the brain, providing connections between various parts of the brain. So we write relay. Leave control and sensory out.

q: The hypothalamus helps regulate the body's internal environment and acts as a major link between the nervous and _____ systems.
e: The hypothalamus helps regulate the body's internal environment and acts as a major link between the nervous and endocrine systems. So we write endocrine. Leave exocrine and lymphatic out.

q: The midbrain plays an important role in eye movement and control of skeletal muscles, and relays visual and _____ information.
e: The midbrain plays an important role in eye movement and control of skeletal muscles, and relays visual and auditory information. So we write auditory. Leave olfactory and gustatory out.

q: The cerebellum is involved in the unconscious coordination of posture, reflexes, and fine, voluntary _____ skills.
e: The cerebellum is involved in the unconscious coordination of posture, reflexes, and fine, voluntary motor skills. The blank is motor. Not sensory or cognitive.

q: The medulla oblongata coordinates automatic bodily functions that maintain homeostasis, including heart rate and the rate and depth of _____.
e: The medulla oblongata coordinates automatic bodily functions that maintain homeostasis, including heart rate and the rate and depth of breathing. So we write breathing. Leave digestion and excretion out.

q: A cross section of the spinal cord reveals an outer white matter consisting of myelinated nerve fibres and a butterfly-shaped core of _____ matter.
e: A cross section of the spinal cord reveals an outer white matter consisting of myelinated nerve fibres and a butterfly-shaped core of white matter. White is the word, not yellow or grey.

q: The somatic nervous system is under voluntary control and includes 12 pairs of cranial nerves and _____ pairs of spinal nerves.
e: The somatic nervous system is under voluntary control and includes 12 pairs of cranial nerves and 31 pairs of spinal nerves. So we write 31. Leave 12 and 43 out.

q: An exception among cranial nerves is the _____ nerve, which connects to many internal organs including the heart, lungs, and digestive tract.
e: An exception among cranial nerves is the vagus nerve, which connects to many internal organs including the heart, lungs, and digestive tract. The blank is vagus. Not optic or olfactory.

q: Sudden, involuntary responses to certain stimuli that enable the body to react rapidly in times of danger are called _____.
e: Sudden, involuntary responses to certain stimuli that enable the body to react rapidly in times of danger are called reflexes. The blank is reflexes. Not instincts or tropisms.

q: Reflex arcs are simple connections of only three neurones to transmit messages, allowing reflexes to occur rapidly in about _____ $	ext{ms}$.
e: Reflex arcs are simple connections of only three neurones to transmit messages, allowing reflexes to occur rapidly in about 50 ext{ms}. 50 is the word, not 20 or 100.

q: The sympathetic nervous system is typically activated in stressful situations, releasing a neurotransmitter called _____ which has an excitatory effect.
e: The sympathetic nervous system is typically activated in stressful situations, releasing a neurotransmitter called norepinephrine which has an excitatory effect. Norepinephrine is the word, not acetylcholine or dopamine.

q: The parasympathetic nervous system acts to restore and conserve energy, and uses the neurotransmitter _____ to control organ responses.
e: The parasympathetic nervous system acts to restore and conserve energy, and uses the neurotransmitter acetylcholine to control organ responses. The blank is acetylcholine. Not dopamine or serotonin.

q: The nervous system is composed of neurones and cells that support them, which are collectively called _____ cells.
e: The nervous system is composed of neurones and cells that support them, which are collectively called glial cells. The blank is glial. Not epithelial or muscle.

q: Dendrites are short, branching terminals that receive nerve impulses, while the _____ conducts impulses away from the cell body.
e: Dendrites are short, branching terminals that receive nerve impulses, while the axon conducts impulses away from the cell body. So we write axon. Leave dendrite and soma out.

q: The axons of some neurones are enclosed in a fatty, insulating layer called the myelin sheath, which is made up of _____ cells.
e: The axons of some neurones are enclosed in a fatty, insulating layer called the myelin sheath, which is made up of endothelial cells. Endothelial is the word, not schwann or glial.

q: Structurally, a multipolar neurone has several dendrites and a single axon, and is typically found in the _____.
e: Structurally, a multipolar neurone has several dendrites and a single axon, and is typically found in the brain and spinal cord. The blank is brain and spinal cord. Not inner ear or peripheral nervous system.

q: Bipolar neurones have a single main dendrite and a single axon, and are found in the inner ear, the retina, and the _____ area of the brain.
e: Bipolar neurones have a single main dendrite and a single axon, and are found in the inner ear, the retina, and the olfactory area of the brain. The blank is olfactory. Not auditory or visual.

q: Functionally, interneurones are found entirely within the central nervous system and act as a link between sensory and _____ neurones.
e: Functionally, interneurones are found entirely within the central nervous system and act as a link between sensory and motor neurones. So we write motor. Leave sensory and autonomic out.

q: The connection between two neurones, or a neurone and an effector, is called a _____.
e: The connection between two neurones, or a neurone and an effector, is called a synapse. The blank is synapse. Not ganglion or node.

q: Chemical messengers called neurotransmitters carry the neural signal across the synapse, taking about $0.5$ to _____ $	ext{ms}$ to reach the postsynaptic membrane.
e: Chemical messengers called neurotransmitters carry the neural signal across the synapse, taking about 0.5 to 1 ext{ms} to reach the postsynaptic membrane. So we write 1. Leave 0.1 and 0.5 out.

q: If a neurotransmitter is excitatory, it triggers ion channels to allow positive ions like _____ to flow into the postsynaptic neurone.
e: If a neurotransmitter is excitatory, it triggers ion channels to allow positive ions like sodium to flow into the postsynaptic neurone. The blank is sodium. Not potassium or calcium.

q: If a neurotransmitter is inhibitory, it triggers channels to allow potassium ions to flow out, resulting in a more negative membrane potential called _____.
e: If a neurotransmitter is inhibitory, it triggers channels to allow potassium ions to flow out, resulting in a more negative membrane potential called hyperpolarization. The blank is hyperpolarization. Not depolarization or repolarization.

q: Excessive production of the neurotransmitter dopamine is linked to _____, a disorder where perception of reality is greatly distorted.
e: Excessive production of the neurotransmitter dopamine is linked to schizophrenia, a disorder where perception of reality is greatly distorted. Schizophrenia is the word, not Parkinson's disease or Alzheimer's disease.

q: Inadequate amounts of the neurotransmitter _____ in the brain synapses are linked to depression.
e: Inadequate amounts of the neurotransmitter serotonin in the brain synapses are linked to depression. The blank is serotonin. Not endorphin or dopamine.

q: Endorphins act as natural painkillers in the brain, and a deficiency is linked to an increased risk of _____.
e: Endorphins act as natural painkillers in the brain, and a deficiency is linked to an increased risk of alcoholism. So we write alcoholism. Leave insomnia and anxiety out.

q: The somatic nervous system's sensory neurones carry information from receptors in the skin, tendons, and skeletal muscles, while its motor neurones carry information to the _____ muscles.
e: The somatic nervous system's sensory neurones carry information from receptors in the skin, tendons, and skeletal muscles, while its motor neurones carry information to the cardiac muscles. The blank is cardiac. Not skeletal or smooth.

q: Unipolar neurones have a single process that extends from the cell body, where the dendrite and axon are fused, and are found in the _____ nervous system.
e: Unipolar neurones have a single process that extends from the cell body, where the dendrite and axon are fused, and are found in the peripheral nervous system. The blank is peripheral. Not central or autonomic.
